values: Test on desktop and phone. Set Status as you go; use Notes / Issue to record anything that needs fixing.
Open the website at / and select the main call to action.
It opens the dashboard without errors.
Every visible item opens a working page; no placeholder page appears.
Mark a title and an episode as watched; return Home.
Watched titles, episodes, favorites, and estimated hours update.
Mark one or more episodes watched.
Recent items appear with correct title and season/episode detail.
Remove the local TMDB key in Settings and browse the app.
Fallback titles and their detail pages still work.
Connect a valid TMDB key in Settings.
The app confirms the connection and shows live content.
Search for a movie and a TV show from the top bar.
Relevant results appear and open the selected title page.
Each list loads and title cards are clickable.
Open a movie and a TV show.
Title, metadata, synopsis, rating controls, and images display cleanly.
Open Watch Trailer, then close it.
The modal opens when a trailer exists and the page remains usable after closing.
State changes correctly and the title appears/disappears from history.
Toggle two episodes watched, refresh, then untoggle one.
Episode state survives refresh and dashboard progress is correct.
Favorite a title; open Favorites; remove it.
The list updates immediately and after refresh.
Rate a title, refresh, then revisit it.
Your score is retained and shown on the title page.
Post a review with a score; refresh.
Review text, score, and date remain visible.
Rated/reviewed titles show correct scores, counts, and links.
Open View History from the dashboard.
Items are newest first and open their title page.
Create a list, change its name/privacy, refresh.
Changes are saved and visible after refresh.
Use Add to List on a title page.
Correct title, year, type, and poster are added to the chosen list.
Add an item manually, then remove it.
The list updates immediately and remains correct after refresh.
Dashboard greeting and new review name use the saved name.
The chosen theme remains active and text stays readable.
Use Clear local data only after testing other rows.
Confirmation appears; app data clears and the app still works.
Test at 375 px width or on a phone.
Navigation is usable, no overlap occurs, and controls can be tapped.
Open a title page on a phone-sized screen.
Poster, action buttons, season list, and review area fit without clipping.
Use Tab / Enter through top navigation and title actions.
Visible focus, logical order, and all important actions can be reached.
Review images, labels, and dark mode.
Images have useful alt text and text remains readable.
Open a bad title URL and disconnect the API.
A clear recovery message and a way back are shown.
Reload on normal and slow network; scroll long pages.
No major delays, broken images, or noticeable interface freezes.
Run npm run build before deployment.
Build finishes with no errors or lint warnings.

values: Use this page after testing to turn findings into a prioritized improvement plan. Add your own ideas below the starter items.
Makes the app comfortable to use on phones and tablets.
Helps users see upcoming episodes and releases.
Turns existing tracking data into useful insights.
Charts for titles, episodes, favorites, and hours.
Protects watched, rating, history, and collection logic from regressions.
Lets people keep their data across browsers and devices.
Avoids exposing a browser API key and enables caching.
Use serverless functions or API server.
Plan to watch, watching, completed, on hold, dropped.
Makes discovery more useful as library data grows.
Brings users back for upcoming episodes and releases.
Makes the project installable and more app-like.
